body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: "Audio on fixed presets is AAC 128 kbps" is now false for YouTube**

This bullet is unchanged, but the YouTube canvases are fixed presets too, and they now target 384 kbps. `resolveExportTarget` picks `YOUTUBE_AUDIO_BITRATE` (384_000) for them in `export-presets.ts:489`, and the table row and the new section in this same doc both say 384 kbps. Suggested wording: "Audio on Vertical and Square is AAC 128 kbps …; YouTube uses 384 kbps (see below)".

🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Wrong claim that upscaling used the default filter before this PR**

The fixed-canvas framer, which upscales YouTube Fit output, already set `imageSmoothingEnabled = true` and `imageSmoothingQuality = "high"` before this PR (`compose-output-frame.ts:213-214` and `:220-221`, untouched here). The code comment this PR adds at `:99` says so too: "as the fixed-canvas framer does". The zoom crop also already had `"high"` quality. This PR only adds `imageSmoothingEnabled = true` there, plus high-quality smoothing for contained slides (`drawContained`). Saying upscaling "now" uses high quality and "used the default filter" before overstates the change: readers will think it explains a visual difference. Suggested wording: "slides drawn onto the canvas now use `imageSmoothingQuality = \"high\"` as well (the framer and zoom crop already did)". For the same reason, the first two tests in `compose-output-frame.test.ts` cover behaviour that existed before this PR, not something it adds.
Fixed in 12d33d10: the bullet now says Vertical and Square use AAC 128 kbps and YouTube uses 384 kbps (see below).

Fixed in 12d33d10: the note now says only slides gained `imageSmoothingQuality = "high"`; the fixed-canvas framer and the zoom crop already had it, so it does not explain the YouTube difference (that is the 1440p/4K upload). The PR body is corrected the same way. The first two tests in `compose-output-frame.test.ts` stay as regression guards for the existing framer behaviour, which the 1440p/4K upscale now depends on.
